title: Libertarian candidate Bill Redpath vies for U.S. Senate
description:
BOARDMAN, Ohio (WKBN) — Ohio’s November election will have three political parties represented in the race for U.S. Senate: a Democrat, a Republican and a Libertarian.

Sherrod Brown and Jon Husted are recognizable, but Bill Redpath is not.

Redpath drove to Youngstown from his home near Toledo to promote his candidacy for the U.S. Senate in Ohio for the Libertarian Party.

“I joined the party in ’84 and became active in ’86,” Redpath said. “We generally take conservative positions on economic issues, generally liberal positions on social issues. But there is a core theme, and that is we believe people ought to be able to live their lives without interference as long as they are not harming other people or their property.”

On social issues, Redpath opposes the war with Iran along with a federal ban on abortion.

He supports a relatively open immigration system and birthright citizenship.

On economic issues, Redpath says Medicare payments should be sent to patients and not hospitals and that Medicaid should be run by the states after a 10-year phase out. He also says Social Security needs reformed.

“I favor a commission that would put forward a series of recommendations to save Social Security and direct it toward the poorer people in society, frankly,” Redpath said.
